purpose: Teach: 好ましい/分かち/動かさ/限る/だまさ/近頃/さよなら/ボロ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫の態度、好ましいな、最近、頼もしくなってきた、本当に。
lines.en: Our grandchild's attitude — it's good. He's become so dependable lately, truly.
lines.style: Quiet appreciation. Slow cadence on the opening phrase. Warm, meditative tone. Voice softens toward 'truly' — the contentment of having watched someone grow.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。私たち、人生、分かち合ってきたわね、半世紀以上、二人で。
lines.en: Yes. We've shared so much life together, haven't we? More than fifty years now, just the two of us.
lines.style: Gentle and affirming. Steady, reflective pace. A small smile in the voice. The quiet satisfaction of looking back at a long partnership without sentimentality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 最近、私、重たい家具、動かさないように、気をつけているよ。
lines.en: I've been careful lately, not lifting heavy furniture anymore. Paying attention to that.
lines.style: Practical but slightly embarrassed. Direct tone — matter-of-fact about aging without making a show of it. A faint note of acceptance underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 年寄りには、温泉に限るわね、お互いに、リフレッシュね。
lines.en: For people our age, there's nothing like a good hot spring. We refresh ourselves there, together.
lines.style: Tender and knowing. Warm, slightly playful. Voice carries the ease of shared routines — not pushing, just agreeing with comfort.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 近所のうわさ、だまされないように、注意しているよ、私たち。
lines.en: I'm careful not to believe every rumor the neighbors spread. We don't let ourselves get fooled.
lines.style: Alert and steady. A hint of dry humor — not bitter, just practiced wisdom. Light conviction without any edge.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 近頃、息子の家、訪ねるの、毎月の、楽しみよ、私の。
lines.en: Visiting our son's house has become something I look forward to every month now. One of my small joys.
lines.style: Warm and intimate. Gentle contentment in the delivery. Voice brightens slightly on 'look forward to' — pride and affection coexist naturally.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の友人と、さよならを告げて、もう、随分経つな、ばあさん。
lines.en: Saying goodbye to old friends — it's been a long time now, hasn't it, dear? So many of them gone.
lines.style: Wistful and reflective. Slow, measured delivery. A catch of tender sadness, not heavy — the acceptance that comes with age. Eyes looking back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の私のミシン、ボロボロになるまで、使ったわよ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Do you remember my sewing machine from when we were young? I used it until it fell apart completely.
lines.style: Wistful and specific. Voice carries the memory gently — not dwelling but not rushing. Slight warmth on 'remember' — inviting him into the recollection with her.
